comments.author: jneumann004
comments.story_title: Ask HN: How to improve vim productivity and workflow?
comments.why_zh: 关于不用插件的 vim 的实用视频
comments.quote_zh: 这里有几个挺实用的 YouTube 视频
comments.text_zh: 用最适合你的编辑器就行。过去两年我几乎每天都用 Vim，已经学会了在里面飞快地干活。至于插件，如果某个听起来有意思或者对你有用，那就装上。要是不好使，之后删掉就行。这些年我把流行的插件都试了个遍，但最终精简到 4 个，外加几个针对特定语言的插件。这里有几个挺实用的 YouTube 视频：Vim Navigation Commands [LINK] How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim) [VIDEO]
comments.text: Use the editor that works best for you. I have used Vim every day for almost the last two years and I have learned to work very quickly inside of it. As far as plugins, if one sounds interesting or useful to you, install it. If it doesn't work out, then you can delete it later. Over the years I have tried all of the popular plugins, but I have managed to whittle it down to 4 plus a couple of language specific plugins Here are a couple of handy youtube videos Vim Navigation Commands [LINK] How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim) [VIDEO]

comments.author: wodny
comments.why_zh: 关于 Vim 内置能力的不错演讲
comments.quote_zh: YouTube 上 Max Cantor 还有一个相当不错的演讲
comments.text_zh: 我认为，如果不真正掌握一些基础概念，比如移动、操作符、寄存器、窗口等，就不可能有好的 vimrc。我最近把 Drew Neil 的 VimCasts[1] 全看了一遍，仅仅几个小时后我就意识到，至少 10 年来我一直漏掉了很多东西。YouTube 上 Max Cantor 的《How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)》[2] 也是一个相当不错的演讲。与其把某个单一的 vimrc 当作最佳配置，不如翻一翻一些有影响力的 Vim 用户，比如 Drew Neil[3] 和 Tim Pope[4] 的 dotfiles 和插件。顺便说一句，VimCasts 还配有一本书。第二版[5]包含了 Vim 8.0 引入的改动。[1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO] [3]: [LINK] [4]: [LINK] [5]: [LINK]
comments.text: I don't believe it's possible to have a good vimrc without really grasping some elementary concepts like movements, operators, registers, windows etc. I have recently watched all the Drew Neil's VimCasts[1] and after just a couple of hours I've realized I was missing a lot for at least 10 years. There is also quite a good presentation on YouTube by Max Cantor "How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)"[2]. Instead of treating a single vimrc as the best one it's useful to skim through dotfiles and plugins of some influential vim users like Drew Neil[3] and Tim Pope[4]. BTW VimCasts are accompanied by a book. The second edition[5] includes changes introduced by Vim 8.0. [1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO] [3]: [LINK] [4]: [LINK] [5]: [LINK]

comments.author: DyslexicAtheist
comments.story_title: Coc.nvim – Intellisense Engine for Vim8 and Neovim
comments.why_zh: 支持极简、不用插件的 vim 思路
comments.text_zh: 有些语言就是比别的更啰嗦。如果你要应付 `ProblemProblemFactory` 那种抽象 madness，并且信奉把每个变量都拼写完整（用 MessageCounter 而不是 "cnt" 之类），那这个看起来会挺方便。也许这是心态和哲学的问题。我个人更喜欢一个极简但强大、不带插件的编辑器，只依赖它自身的能力（当然这有学习曲线）。这样在别人的机器上执行 $EDITOR foo 时不会卡住，依然感觉自在，速度也和在主工作环境里一样。"如何用纯 Vim 实现插件 90% 的功能"：[视频]
comments.text: some languages are more verbose than others. if you're dealing with `ProblemProblemFactory` type of abstraction madness and subscribe to the idea of spelling out every variable (MessageCounter instead of "cnt" etc) then this would seem handy. Maybe it's a question of mindset & philosophy. I personally prefer a minimalist but powerful editor without plugins and just rely on their internal capabilities (which granted are a learning curve). It avoids getting stuck when doing $EDITOR foo on a system you don't own and still feel at home and as fast as on your primary workspace. "How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)" : [VIDEO]

comments.author: noud
comments.why_zh: 相关的原生 Vim 用法演讲
comments.quote_zh: 另外相关的是，How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)
comments.text_zh: 难道只有我在用极简配置（不到 50 行）的原生 Vim 吗？我把 tab 设为 4 个空格、打开语法高亮、把背景设为深色、加上模糊查找，再配置 netrw（默认的文件浏览）。设置非常简单。而且，当我在别的电脑上打开（原生）Vim 而没有任何配置时，我知道一切都和我的默认 Vim 环境大体一致。我觉得在默认的 Vim 环境里做开发并不难，只需做些小调整。另外相关的是，How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Am I the only one using vanilla vim with a minimal configuration file (<50 lines)? I set tabs to 4 spaces, put syntax highlighting on, set background to dark, add fuzzy finding, and configure netrw (default file browsing). Very easy to setup. Moreover, when I'm on a different computer and open (vanilla) vim without any configurations. I know that everything is more or less the same as my default vim environment. I think it's not that hard to learn developing in the default vim environment, with some minor tweaks. Also related, How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim): [VIDEO]

comments.author: gregjor
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Alternative to VS Code?
comments.why_zh: 有趣地一窥 vim 功能如何替代 IDE 的额外功能
comments.text_zh: > 自动补全，以及通过点击函数在代码中导航（甚至是我依赖项的代码），还有弹出层显示我要调用的函数的文档/签名。这些是我还没准备放弃的体验优化功能。ctags 几十年前就做到了其中大部分。普通 vim 就有不错的自动补全和签名弹窗，也能导航到函数和类定义。不需要 LSP。LSP 会做得更好，但有时开销相当大。正如我提到的，我不用 VSCode 或 JetBrains IDE。我知道它们，也用过。我的配置是语言无关的，而且我也会用多种语言工作。可能有用，至少有意思：[VIDEO]
comments.text: > The ability to autocomplete, and navigate through the code (even my dependencies's code) by the click on a function, the popover showing the documentation/signature of the function i'm going to call. Those are Quality of Life features I'm not ready to give up on. ctags did most of that decades ago. Plain vim has good autocomplete and signature popovers, along with navigating to functions and class definitions. No LSP needed. An LSP will do it better but with sometimes significant overhead. As I noted I don't use VSCode or a JetBrains IDE. I know about them and have used them. My setup works language-agnostic, and I also work in multiple languages. Possibly useful, at least interesting: [VIDEO]

comments.author: skydhash
comments.story_title: OpenVSX, which VSCode forks rely on for extensions, down for 24 hours
comments.why_zh: 关于不用插件的 vim 的不错演讲
comments.quote_zh: 一个不错的演讲，即使讲的是 vim
comments.text_zh: 用 vim、neovim、emacs 这类编辑器，先摸清整体情况（看教程、把默认配置玩一玩……）然后列出你需要什么，会容易得多。我的 vim 配置只有三样东西：LSP、FZF（用于任何模糊查找）和 Plug（用来安装上面两个）。也还有一些锦上添花的东西，但我可以不要它们，或者把它们并入主配置。但它不是我的日常编辑器，所以那只是基础配置。在此基础上我能加的任何东西，都取决于我要用它来做哪些项目。那大约 200 行（LSP 配置占其中四分之一）。注意：一个不错的演讲，即使讲的是 vim，“How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)” [VIDEO]
comments.text: With editors like vim, neovim, emacs, it's way easier to get the lay of the land first (tutorial, play around with the default config,..) and then list out what you need. My vim config has three things only: LSP, FZF (for anything fuzzy), and Plug (to install the above two). There's also a few niceties, but I could do without them. or vendor them into the main config. But it's not my daily editor, so that's just the base config. Anything I could add on top of that would depend on the projects I would need it for. That's about 200 lines (the lsp config is 1/4 of that) NB. A nice talk even if it's about vim "How to Do 90% of What Plugins Do (With Just Vim)" [VIDEO]
